added_failures_note: from the reviewed run's own arm logs: logs/base-arm.log (revision eca5c58dc8) fails 3 ids and logs/head-arm.log (revision 19746f319) fails 4; the set difference is the single id above, which passes 5 of 5 alone runs in both arms (logs/alone-base.log, logs/alone-head3.log).

findings.text: the age fallback now reads a field the snapshot does not carry, so it silently reports zero. `entered = _created_seconds(snapshot, moment=at)` is handed the watch snapshot, but `_created_seconds` reads `pointer.get("created_at")` (reckon/crew/needs_you.py:97) and `_compute_watch_snapshot` returns an explicit dict with no `created_at` key (reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:1214-1310), so the stamp is always absent and the fallback returns `moment`, giving age_seconds 0.0. The base revision passed the pointer (`entered = _created_seconds(pointer, moment=at)` before 19746f319) and read the real creation instant, so this is a regression in the reviewed diff. It is reachable exactly for the population the module exists to name: `_state_entered_seconds` returns None whenever the run has no stream (reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:1196-1198 leaves stall_stream_path None) or no transition to its current state, and a stalled run has no `blocked` transition to find — which the module's own docstring anticipates, as a run may be in a needs-action state whether or not a producer ever wrote a transition for it. The effects: the pane prints `fsa-repair 0m` for a run that has been blocked for hours, and the oldest-first sort at reckon/crew/needs_you.py:176 orders by that same broken number, so the row that most needs attention sinks to the bottom of its group.

`_snapshots` duplicates a mapping the repository already builds. reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:2211-2229 (`_live_project_session_counts`) lists the same live pointers, reduces each through the same `_watch_snapshot` over the same `parse_duration(DEFAULT_WATCH_STALL_WINDOW)`, and keys them by the same stringified run id, then hands them straight to `_fleet_counts`; the added helper is that expression minus the counting. It does not extend that owner, and the owner could be rewritten onto it as `_fleet_counts(_snapshots(...), session=...)`, so the two are free to drift on the run-id keying and the stall window. Not blocking: the behaviour matches today, and the searched neighbour is the only other expression of this map in reckon/crew.

the new default arms the emitter on every follower in the fleet, and the one id the population gained at head is the only end-to-end test of a real follower process. `needs_scan_seconds` is min(interval, FOLLOWER_SETTLE_SAMPLE_SECONDS=1.0) (reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:2141-2145), so an armed follower now composes the needs-you summary from the project's live pointers once a second where it previously did nothing; logs/head-arm.log fails tests/test_a_pane_settles_when_no_work_is_live.py::test_the_real_follower_settles_when_the_host_advertises_it on its 20 s settle timeout while logs/alone-base.log and logs/alone-head3.log pass it 5 of 5 alone in both arms, and the head arm took 401 s against the base arm's 254 s. Attribution to load is plausible but unproven from two arms that ran at different times on a shared node; what is not in doubt is that the change adds per-second work to every follower and no arm measured that cost. Worth a follow-on: re-run the two arms interleaved, or move the scan behind the change check.
